### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0c7e95aff5996de2313b4668760eafee2e50172d`.

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0c7e95aff5996de2313b4668760eafee2e50172d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8f5ff65b5fad97d9109a3ad2f58c0025b5d0c3ae` — the merge of head `e16fea955b42696bbbe6258047ad8aaf57767e8c` into base `0c7e95aff5996de2313b4668760eafee2e50172d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8f5ff65b5fad97d9109a3ad2f58c0025b5d0c3ae && git checkout 8f5ff65b5fad97d9109a3ad2f58c0025b5d0c3ae
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0c7e95aff5996de2313b4668760eafee2e50172d e16fea955b42696bbbe6258047ad8aaf57767e8c && git checkout -B drift-repro 0c7e95aff5996de2313b4668760eafee2e50172d && git merge --no-ff e16fea955b42696bbbe6258047ad8aaf57767e8c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0c7e95aff5996de2313b4668760eafee2e50172d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0c7e95aff5996de2313b4668760eafee2e50172d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4960c1d3e5c8ade07432fdb50ddb7047ff82b19e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: the PR diff against merge-base `c58008187f` (all 5 files, 2 commits); `packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts` at head (`SNAKE_CASE` :27, the three new constants :148-176, `BlueprintViewSchema` :192-215 with `startDateField` :212-213, the widget :236-250 with `measure` :241-242 and `aggregate` :243-244, the cloud#1967 notes :270-278 and :376-384, `strictIdent` / `strictIdentOrNull` :385-388, `StrictView` :474-494 with `startDateField` :493, `StrictDashboard` widget :496-512 with `measure` :504 and `aggregate` :508-509, `SolutionBlueprintSchema` :324, `SolutionBlueprintStrictSchema` :561); `packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.test.ts` at head (view parity :898-911, dashboard and widget parity :913-930, VALUE-parity walker :1051-1118, the new describe :1173-1296); `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json` (:46-48, :65, :86-88); `content/docs/references/ai/solution-blueprint.mdx` at head (:86-97, :272-300, strict views and dashboards sections); `.changeset/30430-blueprint-widget-aggregate-calendar-date.md`; `packages/spec/liveness/README.md` :27-70; `packages/spec/scripts/liveness/check-liveness.mts` (`GOVERNED` :281, `SPEC_ONLY_SCHEMAS` :481-484); `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json` (`ai/BlueprintView` :32-36); `packages/spec/scripts/check-llms-txt.ts` (count semantics :56, :179); `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` :905-930; `AGENTS.md` Prime Directives #10 and #12 (:264-283); the order `/mnt/project-files/seat3-orders/30430.md`; card #30430 body and 4 comments (os-dev-report 6658975093 included); PR #30484 body, 2 comments, 0 reviews; check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Value parity holds and is pinned. Both sides spell one module-local tuple `BLUEPRINT_WIDGET_AGGREGATES` (:156) through `z.enum(...)`, `.optional()` on the lenient widget (:243) and `.nullable()` on the strict widget (:508), so the enum values cannot differ; `startDateField` is `z.string().regex(SNAKE_CASE).optional()` on the lenient view (:212) and `strictIdentOrNull(...)` on the strict view (:493), the same `SNAKE_CASE` pattern the VALUE-parity walker indexes on both sides (walker :1072-1104 treats optional / nullable / lazy as transparent and records string leaves by path, so `views[].startDateField` is compared). The walker returns on enums (:1099-1100), so `aggregate` was outside it; the new widget-parity pin closes that with an explicit options comparison (:929-930). Key parity: the VIEW pin (:909-910) now requires `startDateField` on both sides, and the new DASHBOARD and WIDGET pin (:913-930) is the first widget-level key-parity pin this file has had (`git diff` confirms none existed at the merge-base). Optional versus nullable is the mirror's standing spelling (:386 "this mirror's spelling of optional"), and the strict fixtures in the file gained both keys (diff :77-80, :88-91, :100).
2. The `measure` describes no longer claim automatic aggregation and carry no title heuristic. Lenient (:241-242): "The field this widget aggregates ... or "count" to count records. Name the FIELD, not "total_amount" or "avg_score": how it is aggregated is what `aggregate` says, never this key ... Omit for a count widget." Strict (:504): the same rule with "or null for a count widget". Gone: "The aggregation is chosen automatically from the field type", "Omit to let the builder infer from the title" (lenient) and "or null to infer from the title" (strict), all three visible as deletions in the diff. The `aggregate` describe (`WIDGET_AGGREGATE_MEANING` :159) names each value's meaning (sum = total of `measure`, avg, min / max, count = number of records after `condition`), states that sum / avg / min / max need a numeric `measure`, and states the count rule ("count" needs no `measure` field ... a field named in `measure` beside it is not read), on both sides through the shared constant. The pin at :1250-1259 reads both describes on both sides and refuses `/infer/i` and `/chosen automatically/i`; it does not refuse `/title/i`, so the rejected option C could return under another verb (should-fix 1). Pre-existing title heuristics on sibling keys remain: widget `groupBy` (:245-246 "the title and this field MUST name the SAME field") and `condition` (:247-248 "when its title implies a threshold or status"); the ruling rejected inferring the AGGREGATION from the title, and the order's ⛔ names "title-based inference" for that slot, so these sit outside the card and are flagged under ③, not owed here.
3. "Ignored, not refused" against Prime Directive #10. The directive's corollary is "never advertise or demo a capability the runtime doesn't actually deliver (declared ≠ enforced) ... keep the claim as narrow as the enforcement", and #12 asks that off-spec metadata be rejected at authoring or publish so the error surfaces loudly. Judged acceptable here, for three reasons the code and body give and one they do not. (a) The claim is as narrow as the enforcement: the describe on both sides says "For type:"calendar" only" and "Ignored on the other view types" (:175, :493 adds "Null on every view that is not a calendar"), so nothing is advertised that the reader does not deliver; the silent no-op is declared, which is the narrowing #10 asks for. (b) The strict mirror is per-leaf JSON Schema (:270-278, :376-384) and cannot state "startDateField only when type is calendar"; a lenient-side `.superRefine` would run at apply only, after the model generated against a mirror that allowed the pairing, which is the cloud#1967 failure this file documents (a blueprint the user approved refused wholesale at apply), and the published JSON Schema would carry it as a dropped refinement (`dropped-refinements.baseline.json` already lists `ai/BlueprintView` for `filters.element`). (c) The same shape already carries a kind-scoped key other kinds ignore: strict `groupBy` :480 "Null for list/form/calendar/gallery", lenient `groupBy` :200-201 "REQUIRED for kanban ... Optional for gantt". (d) What is missing is the loud signal #12 wants at the one place a cross-key rule can be stated, the reader (cloud#3607's compile): the dev recorded both pairings as carrier notes in the os-dev-report's `out_of_scope_findings` (sum / avg / min / max without a numeric measure; `startDateField` on a non-calendar view) but the PR body's acceptance notes do not carry them and nothing names them on cloud#3607 yet (should-fix 4). Same verdict for `measure` beside `aggregate: 'count'`: the describe says the field is not read (:159), the per-leaf limit is the same, and the reader is where a refusal belongs. Refusing on the lenient side would make a generated proposal illegal to apply, the worse failure; ignoring with a stated scope is the right choice at this layer.
4. Liveness: outside the ledger, as claimed. The README's denominator is the registered kinds (`BUILTIN_METADATA_TYPE_SCHEMAS`) union `listUnregisteredKindSchemaTypes()` union the `SPEC_ONLY_SCHEMAS` overrides (:27-70); `GOVERNED` (`check-liveness.mts` :281) and `SPEC_ONLY_SCHEMAS` (:481-484: `webhook`, `query`, `validation`) name no blueprint, `git grep -i blueprint packages/spec/src/kernel/` and `grep -ril blueprint packages/spec/liveness/` both return nothing. No row is owed; the order said to say so in the body and add none, and the body does (§ Liveness). Nearest precedent is `query`, a request surface governed by override (README :62-70); the blueprint is cloud's I/O contract with no reader in this repo (`git grep` at head outside the schema and its test hits only `PROTOCOL_MAP.md`, generated ledgers and `ai/index.ts`), so an override would govern a surface whose only consumer is in another repo; not owed by the order.
5. Declarations and ripples. PR body and changeset both carry `Clause-②: yes (widening: ...)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`; the changeset grades `@objectstack/spec` `minor`, the level `added` owes (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs` :909 "added / narrowed / semantic -> at least one moved package minor+"), and `Check Changeset` is green on the head. Ripples: `authorable-surface/ai.json` gains exactly `ai/BlueprintView:startDateField` (:65); the widget is an inline `z.object` under `ai/BlueprintDashboard:widgets` (:48) and the ledger lists no nested widget keys at the merge-base either (`BlueprintWidgetCondition` has rows :86-88 because it is an exported schema), so no `aggregate` row is expected. `content/docs/references/ai/solution-blueprint.mdx` carries the three new or changed rows with describe text byte-equal to the zod constants (lenient widget :94-95, lenient view :300, strict view :429); the strict dashboards section renders `widgets` as a truncated inline type, so no strict widget row is expected there. `api-surface/` and `llms.txt` are untouched and should be: the tuple and the three describe constants are not exported, and `check-llms-txt.ts` re-derives per-module counts over `*.zod.ts` (:179), and no module was added. `Lint · docs & code guards` and `Lint · ESLint` are green on the head; `check:docs` and `check:authorable-surface` exit 0 by the dev's gates report (102 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED).
6. Pins are real by reading. Ablation 1 (strict `aggregate` renamed): `strictWidget(...)` writes `aggregate`, so every strict parse either strips it (the `.toBe(aggregate)` expectations at :1217 and :1220 fail) or reports the renamed required key missing (the single-issue expectations at :1233, :1235 and :1247 fail); the widget key-parity pin fails on key sets; the no-title pin throws reading `.description` of a missing key. Eleven reds of 85 is consistent with that count. Ablation 2 (lenient `startDateField` renamed): the VIEW parity pin (:909-910), the calendar accept pin (:1263-1266 reads `.startDateField` off a lenient parse that now strips it) and the wrong-type pin (:1274-1277 expects an issue at `startDateField`, none now) go red; the non-calendar pin stays green because an unknown key is stripped, which the body states. Three reds, as reported. The unknown-value pin covers `average`, `median`, `count_distinct`, `AVG` and `''` on both sides with exactly one issue at the key (:1230-1237); absent / null / missing are each pinned (:1239-1248); the five non-calendar types are each pinned on both sides (:1285-1295). Gap: the no-title pin's vocabulary (should-fix 1).
7. Body matches code and the order. Every describe the body quotes is in the file verbatim ("Ignored on the other view types (a gantt view takes its dates from `columns`, start before end)", "Null on every view that is not a calendar."); the count rule and the non-calendar choice are stated with reasons in the describe, the file's docblocks (:148-176) and the body, as the order required; `strictIdentOrNull` is what the strict view uses (:493); the five values are the ruling's five and `count_distinct` is named as not offered. One body-versus-code nit: the acceptance notes say the describe "does not describe cloud's default table, which this repo cannot read", while the strict `aggregate` describe (:509) and the lenient one (:244) both assert the fallback "(a numeric field sums)" (should-fix 3). Scope: the four work items of the order are all delivered and nothing outside them moved (5 files, 219 added, 10 deleted, no cloud, no runtime, no ADR); ADR-0087 not needed, as the order said; the `Prior rulings read:` line and `Skills-docs:` line are present; the PR is a draft with no assignees or reviewers.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` minor. Two optional keys are added to a published authorable shape (one new `authorable-surface` row), every existing blueprint parses unchanged, and no value, default or refusal narrows. The strict mirror now requires the two keys of a model generating against it (nullable), which is the mirror's standing contract, not a published-metadata narrowing. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` with `Metadata-protocol: added` is the right pair and the changeset grades the one moved package `minor`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Two spellings of a count widget now coexist on the lenient and strict `measure` describes ('or "count" to count records' at the start, 'Omit for a count widget' / 'or null for a count widget' at the end). `measure: "count"` is kept for existing blueprints and cloud's reader; retiring the literal is a later narrowing with its own ADR-0087 disposition, not this PR's. Until then the describe should say which spelling to write (should-fix 2).
- The reader-side signal for a misplaced `startDateField` or a sum / avg / min / max with no numeric `measure` lives in cloud#3607's compile. The dev filed both as carrier notes on the os-dev-report only; they are not on cloud#3607 (should-fix 4).
- Sibling widget keys `groupBy` (:245-246) and `condition` (:247-248) still carry title-reading guidance that predates this PR and sits outside ruling C's slot (aggregation). No change owed by this card; the seat may want a card if the maintainer reads option C's rejection as shape-wide.
- The `BlueprintViewParsed` and `BlueprintViewSchema.type` default (`list`) are untouched; a lenient view with `startDateField` and no `type` parses as a list that ignores the key, which the describe covers ("Ignored on the other view types").
- Required CI contexts (`Build Core`, `Test Core` 1-8, `Type Check`, the remaining `Lint` shards) were `in_progress` at review time; `Check Changeset`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Spec property liveness` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green. No governed surface in the file list.

### ④ Design judgment

The change is at the right layer and in the right shape: one tuple and three describe constants declared once and read by both the lenient schema and the strict mirror, so the two describes cannot drift; key parity and enum-option parity pinned where the existing VALUE walker is blind; the cross-key rules stated where the contract can state them (the describe and the docblocks) and left to the reader where it cannot (the per-leaf mirror), with the reasoning written beside the code. No must-fix. Should-fix, in order: (1) extend the no-title-inference pin (:1250-1259) to refuse `/title/i` on the `measure` and `aggregate` describes of both sides, so the rejected option C cannot return under another verb; (2) in `WIDGET_MEASURE_RULE` or the lenient / strict `measure` describe, mark `measure: "count"` as the legacy spelling kept for existing blueprints and `aggregate: "count"` as the one to write, and say what a reader does with `measure: "count"` beside `sum` / `avg` / `min` / `max` (no field to aggregate, refused or reported by the reader), so the model has one target; (3) either drop "(a numeric field sums)" from the two `aggregate` describes (:244, :509) or cite it as measured on cloud#3607 (`defaultAggregateFor`, card body), so the describe does not assert a reader behaviour this repo cannot verify and the body's "does not describe cloud's default table" becomes true; (4) carry the two carrier notes from os-dev-report 6658975093 onto objectstack-ai/cloud#3607 as the cloud half's acceptance (a per-widget diagnostic for sum / avg / min / max without a numeric `measure`, and a per-view diagnostic for `startDateField` on a non-calendar view or naming a field that is not date / datetime), which is the loud reader-side refusal Prime Directive #12 asks for and the only place the cross-key rule can be stated. None blocks landing; landing waits on the running required contexts going green.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：AI 蓝图的仪表盘组件新增可选 `aggregate`（`sum` / `avg` / `min` / `max` / `count`），蓝图视图新增可选 `startDateField`（日历视图按哪个日期字段排程，对应建出视图的 `calendar.startDateField`）。宽松 schema 与给模型用的严格镜像两侧同时加，严格侧可为 null。`measure` 的说明改为「只写字段，怎么聚合看 `aggregate`」，删掉了「按字段类型自动选」和「从标题推断」两句，并标明 `measure: "count"` 是旧写法、应写 `aggregate: "count"`。
- 为什么改：执行 cloud#3607 两条裁决（行 2 选 A、日历键选 B）。原来组件只能写 `measure`，平台按字段类型自动聚合，数字字段一律求和，「平均面试评分」显示成 12 个分数之和 908；日历视图也无处写日期字段。
- 风险与回滚：纯增可选键，旧蓝图原样解析；严格镜像只是模型的结构化输出契约，模型此后每个组件 / 视图都要给出这两个键（可为 null）。本仓无读者，读者是 cloud 半（cloud#3607 跟进）。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts` 顶部新增的 `WIDGET_AGGREGATE_MEANING` / `VIEW_START_DATE_FIELD_RULE` 两段说明文字（模型读的就是它们），以及组件 `measure` / `aggregate` 两行；`packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.test.ts` 末尾新增的 describe 块。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/ai/solution-blueprint.test.ts`，预期 85 例全绿（含五个聚合值两侧都收、未知值两侧都拒、非日历视图上的 `startDateField` 被接受而不读）。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

席位意见：fable 契约复审一轮 PASS，无必改；四条建议全部采纳。宽松侧不对「非日历视图写 `startDateField`」或「sum/avg/min/max 缺数字 `measure`」报错，因为严格镜像是逐叶 JSON Schema 表达不了跨键规则，宽松侧拒会让用户已批准的蓝图在应用时整体失败（cloud#1967 那类）；这两条改由 cloud#3607 的编译阶段按组件 / 视图报错，已写进 PR 正文的 Carried 行。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:spec#3 · head `e16fea955b42696bbbe6258047ad8aaf57767e8c`

- **Shape:** 5 files (+220 −10), all under `packages/spec` plus the regenerated reference page, on merge-base `c5800818`: `BLUEPRINT_WIDGET_AGGREGATES` and the shared describe constants (`WIDGET_AGGREGATE_MEANING`, `WIDGET_MEASURE_RULE`, `VIEW_START_DATE_FIELD_RULE`) read by both the lenient schema and the strict mirror; optional `aggregate` on the widget and `startDateField` on the view (nullable on the strict side); key-parity and enum-option-parity pins; a spec minor changeset.
- **Premise measured:** at merge-base a widget could only write `measure` and the reader chose the aggregation from the field type, and a blueprint view had no calendar date key (cloud#3607's rulings: row 2 A, calendar key B).
- **Gates:** at `e16fea95`, full build 119/119, spec 814 files (25610 passed), typecheck exit 0, blueprint pins 85/85, 102/102 derived gates exit 0 and `--ran` reconciles with 0 NOT-MEASURED, `check-changeset-no-major` exit 0 with this body (the `none` control exits 1) (dev report). Check-runs on this head: 57 success, 10 skipped, 0 red; the body edit re-runs the body guards.
- **Contract review:** 6659170858 on `4960c1d3`: PASS, no must-fix. The seat read the round-1 delta (3 files, +6 −5, describes and one pin line only): should-fix 1, the no-title pin now refuses `/title/i` on the `measure` and `aggregate` describes of both sides; should-fix 2, `WIDGET_MEASURE_RULE` names `measure:"count"` as the legacy spelling, says to write `aggregate:"count"`, and says a reader refuses `measure:"count"` beside sum/avg/min/max; should-fix 3, both `aggregate` describes drop "(a numeric field sums)" and say only "the reader's own default"; should-fix 4, the PR body's `Carried:` line gives cloud#3607's cloud half its two acceptance items.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, `@objectstack/spec` minor. ADR-0087 not needed.
- **Accepted deviations:** `startDateField` on a non-calendar view and a sum/avg/min/max widget without a numeric `measure` are declared as ignored / incomplete in the describes, not refused by the schema; the refusal belongs to the reader (cloud#3607), stated in the body.
- **Carried:** objectstack-ai/cloud#3607 (cloud half): (1) a sum/avg/min/max widget whose `measure` is absent, `"count"` or non-numeric is refused per widget, never summed as a record count; (2) `startDateField` is read on calendar views only, and one naming no date/datetime field is refused, never replaced by the first date field.
- **Landing:** not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 30484`: 230 lines). The hand-off is `pr_ready` plus `automerge_enable`, through the merge queue.
